where: the RECENT list of 24 rows below the sticky search band, and the same rows in roster-search
finding: The list is sorted by a key the counselor cannot see, and it is not the key the rest of the app uses. Check-in is sorted by surname; the student directory two tabs away is sorted by given name; and every row in both prints the given name first, in the same weight as the surname. So a counselor with 'Marcus' in front of them scans the leading word down the column and reads Maya, Andre, Chloe, Ruby, Marcus, Layla, Noah, Leila, Diego — no order at all — and cannot jump to a region of the list the way an A–Z list is supposed to let them. They either thumb all 24 rows or give up and type, which is the fallback scene, not the main one. Three seconds per student assumes the eye can land near the right place on the first flick.
evidence: roster--phone.html row order is strictly surname A–Z: Adebayo, Beaulieu, Bergman, Castellanos, Delgado, Farouk, Fitzgerald, Haddad, Herrera, Johnson, Kim, Kowalski, Lindqvist, Mensah, Nguyen, Okafor, Osei, Patel, Petrova, Rahman, Ramirez, Schmidt, Tanaka, Weiss. students--phone.html is strictly given-name A–Z: Aisha, Amara, Ana Lucia, Andre, Brandon, Bree, Caleb, Camila, Chloe, Diego… — the same 45 people, the other key. In the frame the whole name is one bold ink-50 run ('Maya Adebayo'), so nothing marks which half is being sorted on. Rows are 60px tall on a 72px pitch and about 7 fit above the fold, so 24 recent names is three and a half screens of scanning; the full roster behind 'Show all 45 students' at y 2,077 is six.
direction: Pick one key for both lists and give the row a visible anchor for it — either lead with the sorted token, or hold the given name and let the surname carry the ink-50 weight with the given name a step back. Nothing here touches the constraint: the order does not change and a check-in still recolours the row where it stands; this is about what the eye lands on as it travels down a column.

where: the Incomplete profiles card, about 2,250 CSS px down the phone page
finding: The card that answers 'who can nobody reach' will not tell the leader who. Every one of the five names is truncated to make room for two badges and a chevron — 'Selah M…', 'Jayden …', 'Bree S…', 'Tomas…', 'Kylie …' — and two of the five give a given name only. On a 45-student roll that is not an identification, so the leader taps into a record to find out who they were looking at, five times, on the one card whose entire output is a list of names to chase. The New faces card two blocks above prints the same people in full ('Selah Mbeki', 'Jayden Rivers'), which is the proof the width is spendable.
evidence: In dashboard--phone-full the name column is clipped at x≈172 CSS. The 'Visitor' badge runs x 179–236, the 'Waiting 16 days' badge x 245–345 and the chevron ends at 362 — about 180px, 46% of the 390px screen, spent on two pieces of metadata, against roughly 110px left for the name. This is the first round the phone -full frames carry the page below the fold, so this card has not been looked at before.
direction: At 390px the name outranks both badges. Give it the line and push the qualifiers onto the meta line already under it ('6th grade · added Jul 26 · waiting 1 day'), or drop the 'Visitor' badge entirely — the card's own subtitle already scopes the list — and let the wait be a number rather than a pill.

where: the fold — New event, the 'Next in each series' card, the TODAY hero, and the first NEXT SEVEN DAYS row clipped by the nav — and the position of PAST GATHERINGS in the full page
finding: Round 1's answer to this scene was a two-column split at lg, so on the phone nothing moved and the finding stands unchanged: the fold still returns zero complete upcoming rows and 'find the gathering from three weeks ago' still costs six flicks past fourteen future ones. It got marginally worse — the renamed 'Next in each series' card picked up a two-line subtitle and chevrons and grew about 20px, which is 20px taken off the only calendar row that was partly visible. Two of this scene's three jobs still cannot be started on the first screen.
evidence: events--phone-fold: 'New event' at y 66–107; the 'Next in each series' card runs y 138–375, i.e. 237px for two rows that confirm work already done; the TODAY hero y 432–674 (242px, the same card the counselor already has on choose-event); 'NEXT SEVEN DAYS' at 717; the first upcoming row starts at 732 and the bottom nav starts at 776, so 44 of its ~93px show and the next row is entirely below. In r01 that row showed 62px. events--phone-full is 3,706 CSS tall and 'PAST GATHERINGS' sits at y 2,522, behind 18 upcoming rows running out to Sun Sep 20, with no search field and no date jump anywhere on the page.
direction: The positional fix the desktop got needs a phone form. An upcoming/past switch in the header, or one continuous list opened at today's position, puts the hunted-through half within a flick. Separately, 237px at the top of the page is spent telling the leader that both series are already scheduled — that is a one-line statement, and it is what holds the calendar under the fold.

where: the sticky search band — the clear-search '×' inside the field and the quick-add '+' immediately right of it
finding: Moving quick-add out of the scroll plane was the right call and the collision with the student rows is gone. What it created is a smaller one: the '+' now sits 9.5px from the field's own clear button, in the top-right corner — the least reachable spot on the screen and therefore the spot where a stretched thumb is least accurate. The two do different things. A counselor who has finished with a result and reaches up to clear the query, and lands 10px right, gets a full-screen 'Add a visitor' form over the queue instead of the roster back.
evidence: The clear button is `size-11` (44×44) at `right-0.5` inside the input, hit box x 276.5–320.5 CSS; the quick-add is `size-12` (48×48) at x 330–378; both centre on y ≈ 163–211. The `flex items-end gap-2` between them measures 9.5px of daylight. Everything else on this band is at x < 322 or is the field itself; nothing else on the roster puts two different consequences that close together.
direction: Keep it out of the scroll plane, but not shoulder to shoulder with the control that undoes a search. Either put real space between them — the band has room at 390px once the placeholder is short — or make quick-add appear where its premise is actually established, in or under an empty/thin result set, since 'this person is not in the list' is something search has just proved.

where: the order of the cards below Missing in action on the phone stack
finding: The desktop two-column split reordered the phone page and pushed one of the leader's three questions further away. 'Who is new' now sits behind the attendance chart rather than in front of it, so on the phone the leader passes a 320px block with no names in it to reach a two-name list they can act on. The chart is the one section on this page nobody phones anybody about, and it is now the gate to one that is.
evidence: dashboard--phone-full: Missing in action ends around y 1,600; the Attendance trend card runs y 1,625–1,900; the 'New faces' heading is at y 1,944 and Incomplete profiles at 2,253. In r01 New faces preceded the chart. changes.json records the swap as 'a mild improvement (a two-name list before a chart)' — the frames show the opposite order, so this looks like a side effect of the lg grid wrapper rather than a choice.
direction: Let the phone column be ordered by question rather than by which desktop column a section landed in: the three name lists (Missing in action, New faces, Incomplete profiles) first, the chart and the one-off summaries after them. This is an order the lg grid can still draw two ways.

where: the header and filter block above the list, y 65 to 390
finding: The import button was demoted in colour but not in space, so the phone cost of the header is exactly what it was: the first student's name is still at y 409 and six of forty-five fit above the nav. The two buttons now carry the same ink-800 treatment and still occupy two lines, which trades one problem for another — nothing on the screen now says which of them is the weekly action and which is the twice-a-year one, and the page's actual instrument, the search field, still reads as the third control down a stack of four.
evidence: students--phone-fold: 'New visitor' 232×44 at y 65–107, 'Add from Planning Center' 237×44 at y 118–160 — 96px for two rare actions, unchanged from r01. Then the 'Search' label at 186, the field at 203–250, the Grade/Status labels at 272 with their selects at 287–333, and two filter chips at 348–390 (41.5px tall, marginally under the 44px floor). First row Aisha Rahman at 409; bottom nav at 776; six rows visible.
direction: The colour half of this landed; the geometry half did not. One line for the two admin actions — they can share a control, or sit under the list rather than over it — and the four stacked filter rows can be three: the search field alone, then grade/status, then chips, or the labels dropped in favour of placeholders. Every 65px recovered is another student on the first screen.

where: the Missing in action rows in the left column, y=358 to the fold and on to y=1510
finding: The frame change gave this card 680px of width and the row did not spend any of it, so the list that is the whole job still arrives four names at a time. Each MIA row is a three-line text block with a fourth line under it holding Call, Text and the phone number, and none of those four lines uses the right half of the row. The leader on a Tuesday morning came to find out whether this is a four-call week or a twelve-call week; the fold answers 'at least four' and makes them scroll for the rest, exactly as it did in round 1. The column split fixed the page and left the row alone — and the row is now the only thing between the leader and all ten names on one screen.
evidence: Left column runs x=256–936 (680px). Rows are 113–118px: dividers at y=358, 476, 589, 711, 836, so Leila, Trevor, Jasmine and Rohan are complete and Ana Lucia's name lands at y=862 with her contact line below the 900px fold — 4 of 10, versus 3.5 of 10 in round 1. On the top line the meta text ends at x=588 and the MISSED badge starts at x=865: 277px of empty row. On the contact line the phone number ends at x=592, leaving 344px. The card is ~1,230px tall for content that measures ~450px wide at its widest point. Below it the Attendance trend runs to y=1890 while the right column has stopped at y=1585, so 448×305px is blank beside it.
direction: Fold the contact line up into the row: name and one meta line on the left, Call/Text and the missed badge pinned right, at roughly 65–70px per row. Ten rows then measure ~700px and the whole list clears the fold under the tiles. The printed phone number is the cheapest thing to drop — Call and Text already carry it, and it is the string that forces the fourth line. Nothing here touches the gathering split or the All/Sunday/Friday filter.

where: the right column — New faces at y=280–580 and Incomplete profiles at y=596 onward, both above the fold
finding: Putting the small lists side by side exposed something the single stacked column had been hiding behind 1,200px of scroll: the same students are in two lists at once, and the two lists prescribe different actions for them. Selah Mbeki and Jayden Rivers appear in New faces with an amber 'Incomplete' badge and a 48px 'Add parent contact' button, and again 320px lower in Incomplete profiles with a 'Waiting 1 day' pill and a chevron. A leader reading down that column to build this week's call list has to work out by name that these are four entries about two people, and that the card literally titled 'Incomplete profiles' is the one that does not offer the fix. Scroll used to make this an inconsistency nobody met; the column makes it a contradiction on the fold, on the screen whose value is that its counts can be trusted.
evidence: Selah Mbeki's name renders at y=376 and again at y=696; Jayden Rivers at y=489 and y=765 — same 448px column, both pairs above the fold. Across the four list sections the page shows 21 entries covering 16 distinct students: Selah and Jayden are in New faces and Incomplete profiles; Trevor Boyd is in MIA (y=499) and Incomplete profiles (y=1019); Bree Sandoval and Tomas Vielle are in Incomplete profiles and in Met once, never since. The tiles above read 10 / 2 / 7, which sums to 19 rows about 14 people.
direction: Decide what a section membership means when a student qualifies for two. Either the smaller card defers ('2 new faces — both already listed under Incomplete profiles'), or the action moves so each person is offered one next step in one place: 'Add parent contact' belongs in the card named after missing contact, and New faces can carry the flag without repeating the row. Do not solve it by re-stacking the columns — the split is the right answer and the duplication was always there.

where: the right-hand Past gatherings column, from the 'Load older gatherings' button at y=1039 down to the bottom of the page at y=2447
finding: The split did its job — three weeks ago is now on the fold instead of 2,500px down — but the two halves are wildly different lengths, so the page trades one kind of emptiness for another. The past column runs out after twelve rows and the upcoming column keeps going for another 1,300px of alternating Friday Fellowship / Sunday School rows out to Sep 20. From the moment the leader scrolls past the first screen, they are reading a 560px list with 560px of flat ink beside it, which is the shape the round-1 critique was about. Nobody's stated job breaks — all three are served on the fold now — but the recurring rows are the bulk of the page and they are the part that got no width.
evidence: Page is 2,447px tall. Right column x=845–1407 (562px); its last row ends at y=1025 and 'Load older gatherings' at y=1039–1083. Left column x=256–816; its last row ends at y=2405. That is 1,322×562px — 54% of the page height with a blank right half. The 16 'Later' rows are 82px each carrying an icon, a title, a date/time/location line and a 'Recurring' badge, for two series that alternate. 'Load older gatherings' — the control for anything before Jun 21 — sits 139px below the 900px fold.
direction: Let the length imbalance be the thing that decides the layout rather than the calendar order. Either the Later group flows into two sub-columns once the past column has ended, or the repeating occurrences collapse to a denser row (one line: date, series, room) so sixteen of them cost 500px instead of 1,300. A month grid is not needed to fix this and was already declined.

where: the directory rows, from y=178 to the bottom of the list at y=2192
finding: The row got shorter without getting denser. It is now 44px tall and 1,152px wide and it carries the same two facts it carried at 65px — a name on the left and a grade pinned at the far right — with about 790px of nothing between them. Sixteen names above the fold instead of nine is a real win for 'find one student among forty-five'; the second clause of the job, 'see who has no parent contact', is still not answerable from the list. The flag exists but it is an inline badge that trails five of the forty-five names at whatever x the name happens to end, so the leader scanning for it is reading a ragged mid-row position rather than a column — in a row that has 790px of unused width sitting right where that column would go.
evidence: Rows are `lg:min-h-11` at a 45px pitch: 200, 245, 290 … 875, sixteen visible before the 900px fold, list ending at y=2192 on a 2,259px page. The name span is `lg:flex-1` (~940px) holding names that measure 100–190px; grade is a fixed `lg:w-28` at x=1266–1378. 'Missing info' badges appear on 5 rows (Bree Sandoval x=510, Jayden Rivers x=443, Kylie Novak x=428, Selah Mbeki x=434, Tomas Vielle x=436) — five different x positions.
direction: Give the flags a fixed column beside the grade so the answer to 'who has no parent contact' is a vertical run rather than a filter click that discards the alphabet. This is a column for a fact already on the row, not a new fact about a minor. If width is still spare after that, two columns of the A–Z list puts all forty-five names on one screen — the roster's 'a tap never moves a row' constraint does not apply here, since a mis-click opens a neighbouring record and costs one Back.

where: the Incomplete profiles rows — the student name against the 'Visitor' and 'Waiting …' badges
finding: In every row of this section the student's name is the only element allowed to shrink, so the name is the one thing that gets cut while its two decorations render in full. 'Selah Mbeki' becomes 'Selah M…', 'Jayden Rivers' becomes 'Jayden …', 'Bree Sandoval' becomes 'Bree S…' — five of five names truncated — while the blue 'Visitor' chip and the amber 'Waiting 16 days' chip beside them are complete and, being filled and coloured, are also the loudest marks in the row. The composition therefore says the badges are the subject and the person is context, which is backwards on a list whose whole purpose is to hand a leader a name to chase.
evidence: dashboard--phone-full.png, the Incomplete profiles list: every one of the five names ends in an ellipsis, four of them inside the first word of the surname; the trailing 'Waiting 1 day' / 'Waiting 16 days' / 'Waiting 22 days' chips and the 'Visitor' chips never truncate. The markup confirms the priority — the name span carries `truncate` while both badges carry `shrink-0`.
direction: The name should be the last thing in the row to give up width, not the first. Let the badges yield — wrap them below the name, park them in the row's trailing column, or drop 'Visitor' here entirely, since this section is about a missing parent contact and visitor status is already stated on the Students page. Whatever else goes, a person's name in a list of people to contact should read whole at 390px.

where: the two meta lines inside each Missing in action row (and the same pattern in New faces and Met once, never since)
finding: Round 1's change removed the duplicated gathering name from the first meta line, which fixed the desktop but left the phone exactly where it was: all ten MIA rows still cut line one mid-value ('Last seen Jun 21, 1…', 'Jun 28, 2…', 'Jul 5, 22…'), each at a different character, so the block ends in a ragged column of ellipses — while line two directly beneath it ('Missing from Sunday School') stops well short of the same column and leaves roughly 105 CSS px of that width unused. A fact is being cut off on the line above a line that had room for it. The same shape recurs in New faces ('Sunday School · Jul 26, 1 …') and Met once, never since ('met at Fall Lock-In · Ju…').
evidence: dashboard--phone-full.png: ten consecutive MIA rows each ending line one in an ellipsis at a different x; 'Missing from Sunday School' beneath each of them ends around x 253 of a 358 CSS px text column. Compare r01 changes.json change 4, which reports the truncation resolved 'in the wider desktop frame'.
direction: The row is packing three facts into a line that only fits two at this width. Either let this line wrap to two lines on the narrow viewport instead of truncating, or move one fact — grade is the least load-bearing of the three and is already on the student's own record — so that the last-seen date, which is the reason the row exists, survives at 390px.

where: the row beneath the event header — the 'Today' badge, the 'Change' link and the date select
finding: One 44px row carries three different control vocabularies and three type sizes: an 11px ringed chip, a 12px bare blue word with no boundary of any kind, and a 16px ringed pill with a native chevron. The two objects that do the same job — get me to a different gathering — are the two that look least alike, and the one with no visible boundary is the one that navigates. The sizing also inverts the page: the select's label is set at 16px, two steps above the badge and only 2px below the H1 that names the gathering, so the switcher is nearly as loud as the thing it switches. This is the residue the r01 disposition explicitly held over — the fix is a shared vocabulary, not a merge.
evidence: roster--phone-fold.png and roster-search--phone-fold.png, the strip between the event header and the search field. Markup: badge `text-[11px] rounded-md ring-1`, 'Change' `text-xs rounded-full` with no ring or fill, select at inherited 16px `rounded-full ring-1`, against an H1 at `text-lg` (18px).
direction: Give the two event-changing controls one shape, one size and one weight so they read as a pair, and let the 'Today' badge stay the odd one out because it is a status and not a control. Whatever they settle on should sit below the H1 in the type hierarchy — the header's job is to say which gathering you are on, and the machinery for changing it is a footnote to that.

where: the second line of each roster row — the allergy badge and the 'x of 3' attendance ratio
finding: Unchanged from round 1 and held over by the disposition. The ratio is set in tabular numerals — someone wanted it to line up — and then its column moves, because the allergy badge is laid out ahead of it in a wrapping flex row. On plain rows '2 of 3' starts at x 80; on the Layla Farouk, Noah Fitzgerald, Sofia Ramirez and Naomi Tanaka rows it starts at x 153. The one number a counselor compares down the list never appears twice in the same place, so the tabular setting buys nothing. And the amber chip is the heaviest, most saturated mark in the row while sitting in its third-rank line, so it out-shouts the student's own name.
evidence: roster--phone-full.png: the '2 of 3' / '3 of 3' run holds a clean left edge for eighteen rows and jumps right on the four rows that carry the Allergy chip.
direction: Give the ratio a fixed position — first on the meta line with badges trailing, or its own column — so it forms a readable vertical run. And let the allergy flag be legible without being the loudest ink in the row: a warning in the quietest line should not outweigh the name in the loudest one.

where: the Next seven days and Later rows — the 'Recurring' badge and the truncated detail line
finding: Seventeen consecutive rows each spend a whole extra line on an identical grey 'Recurring' chip, and on the line above it each row truncates the only fact that varies ('· Fellowshi…', '· Educa…'). A badge that every row carries is not information, it is a repeated word, and here it is a repeated word that costs a line of height per row and roughly doubles the length of the Later list — while the one row that is genuinely different, Winter Retreat with its One-off and RSVP-only chips, has to compete with sixteen decoys wearing the same badge shape. The row is spending its width on a constant and cutting a variable.
evidence: events--phone-full.png: from Aug 7 to Sep 20 every row shows the same 'Recurring' pill on its own line beneath a detail line that ends in an ellipsis; Winter Retreat's distinguishing chips sit in the middle of that run and read as one more badge.
direction: Mark the exception, not the rule. Drop the badge from recurring rows and let One-off / RSVP only be the only chips in the list, which is both truer and lets the reclaimed line either close up the rows or hold the location that is currently being cut.

where: the 'Next in each series' card heading against the TODAY / NEXT SEVEN DAYS / LATER labels
finding: The page has two heading systems and the wrong one is louder. Four sections are introduced by a 12px bold uppercase label in ink-400; the fifth — a scheduling-maintenance card — is introduced by a 16px semibold card title in ink-100 inside a bordered header, and it sits first on the page. So the biggest, brightest, closest-to-the-reader section heading on Events belongs to the card you touch when you notice something is missing, and tonight's gathering is announced by a grey whisper below it. Squinting at the fold, the composition reads: page title, big card, faint label, hero. That ranks the card above the hero.
evidence: events--phone-fold.png: 'Next in each series' at 16px ink-100 with a rule beneath it, versus 'TODAY' at 12px uppercase ink-400 directly above the hero card; the hero's own title does not appear until y 457 CSS.
direction: Pick one heading system for the page's sections and let every section wear it, so the card stops out-ranking the hero by virtue of being a card. If the series card is genuinely secondary — and its position suggests otherwise — it should also sit below the gathering that is on tonight, not above it.

where: the page header — 'Students / 45 students' against the two stacked action buttons
finding: The header is now a staircase of two same-weight grey buttons hanging off the right edge on two lines, with left edges at x 252 and x 136 and a shared right edge at x 374, beside a title block anchored at x 16. Nothing in the header shares an edge with anything else, and the second button's line runs into the 'Search' label's space below it. Round 1 correctly demoted the import, but demoting both actions to the same treatment has also removed any statement of which one a leader does weekly — and it puts this page out of step with its sibling, where Events gives 'New event' the brand fill. Two core-team pages, the same kind of create action, opposite treatments.
evidence: students--phone-fold.png: 'New visitor' and 'Add from Planning Center' render in identical `bg-ink-800 ring-ink-700` at 14px, right-aligned on two lines; events--phone-fold.png shows 'New event' brand-filled in the same header position.
direction: Let the header resolve to one line — a single visible action with the rare import moved into an overflow, or both actions given a common left edge below the title rather than a right-aligned staircase. And settle one rule across the core-team pages for what a create action looks like, so 'New visitor' and 'New event' are recognisably the same kind of thing.

where: the directory rows that carry Visitor / Missing info badges
finding: Five rows in forty-five wrap their badges onto a second line, which pushes the grade down to a third and makes those rows visibly taller than their neighbours. The grade is the one fact every row shares, and it is the fact whose vertical position moves — so the column that should form a clean run down the list breaks five times. Meanwhile the right two-thirds of every row is empty: the name block ends around x 125 and the chevron sits alone at x 358, so the badges are being stacked into the crowded left column while 230 CSS px of the same row sits unused.
evidence: students--phone-full.png: the Bree Sandoval, Jayden Rivers, Kylie Novak, Selah Mbeki and Tomas Vielle rows are three lines tall with 'Missing info' on its own line and the grade beneath it, against two-line rows everywhere else; the empty middle of every row is the same width in both cases.
direction: Keep the grade on the same line in every row so the list has one rhythm and one column of grades, and let the badges occupy the empty span before the chevron instead of wrapping under the name. Badges should annotate the row, not restructure it.

where: the 'Incomplete profiles (5)' and 'Visitors (5)' quick-filter chips
finding: These two chips print their counts in parentheses inside the label, while every other count in the app is a pill set beside the label — 'Recent 24' and 'Checked in 3' on the roster, 'RESULTS 9' on search, 'Missing in action 10', 'New faces 2' and 'Incomplete profiles 5' on the dashboard. One of those dashboard headings is even the same phrase as the chip here, printed the other way. It is a small thing, but it is the kind of small thing that makes a design system read as a set of pages rather than one app, and the parenthetical form also buries the number in a run of 12px text where the pill form keeps it findable.
evidence: students--phone-fold.png ('Incomplete profiles (5)', 'Visitors (5)') against roster--phone-fold.png ('Recent' + a 24 bubble, 'Checked in' + a 3 bubble) and dashboard--phone-full.png ('Incomplete profiles' + a 5 pill).
direction: Use one form for a count everywhere it appears. The pill is the established one and it is the one that survives a glance; the parentheses should go.

where: the two-column grid below the fold — the tail of 'Later' against the bottom of 'Past gatherings'
finding: The split fixed the fold and re-created the old problem underneath it. The right column is bounded — twelve gatherings and a 'Load older gatherings' button — while the left column is unbounded, because 'Later' is sixteen rows and growing. The columns are sized by whatever their content happens to be and nothing reconciles them, so the page ends on a 560px-wide, 1,305px-tall panel of flat ink-950 beside a narrow column of cards. That is more than a full screen of the exact composition round 1 set out to kill: a phone-width column with the rest of the laptop painted empty. A reader who scrolls past the fold watches the page collapse back into one column and has no way to know the layout ever had two.
evidence: Last ink in the right column is y=1086; last ink in the left is y=2391; the page is 2,447px tall. So for 55% of the page's height the right half of the frame holds nothing at all. The sixteen 'Later' rows are 95px each and fifteen of them carry an identical grey 'Recurring' chip on a line of its own, which is where roughly 400px of that length comes from — a badge that is on every row is not a badge, it is a column of noise that is making the imbalance worse.
direction: A two-column page has to hold for its whole length, not just its first screen. Two ways out and they combine: let the past column keep going (it has 27 gatherings and stops at 12, so it is short by choice, not by content), and stop 'Later' being an unbounded scroll — it is the least urgent block on the page and it is the one setting the page's height. On the row itself, the constants ('Recurring', the venue, the time) repeat identically down fifteen rows while only the date changes; constants belong to the group heading, not to every row, and pulling them up would shorten the column and let the date lead.

where: 'Past gatherings' and 'July 2026' against 'Next in each series' and 'Today' / 'Next seven days' / 'Later'
finding: The split promoted 'Past gatherings' to the title of half the page and left it dressed as the smallest label on it. It is set exactly like 'Today', 'Next seven days' and 'Later' — which are groups *inside* the other column — and one hairline above 'July 2026', which is nested *inside it*. Meanwhile 'Next in each series', a two-row card, is by a distance the loudest section heading on the screen: sentence case, semibold, near-white, wrapped in a ringed container. So the page's three ranks (which half, which group, which month) are carried by two treatments, the largest block has the quietest label and the smallest has the loudest, and the two ranks that are genuinely nested are separated by 1px of size and one step of grey. Nothing on the page says 'upcoming' and 'past'; the columns simply start, in two different idioms, and read as two documents pushed together rather than one page in two parts.
evidence: At the top of the frame the left column opens with a ringed card, a 16px semibold near-white title and a 14px explainer; the right column opens at the same y with a 12px uppercase tracked grey caption, a second 11px uppercase grey caption, and then bare rows sitting flush at the column edge with no container at all. 'Past gatherings' owns 27 rows and is quieter than 'Next in each series', which owns two. choose-event runs the same two systems for the same pair of ranks ('On today' against 'CATCH UP').
direction: Three ranks want three treatments, and the loudest should belong to the halves. Give each column a heading of its own rank at its top so the reader is told what the left/right division means, then use one voice for the groups inside them — either bring 'Next in each series' down into the uppercase group vocabulary or take all four groups up into the card vocabulary, but not both on one page. The nested month labels then need to sit clearly below whatever the group rank becomes.

where: the right column — 'New faces', 'Incomplete profiles', 'Met once, never since' — and the INCOMPLETE tile above it
finding: One fact now wears five costumes inside one 450px column: an amber numeral in the INCOMPLETE tile, an amber '⚠ Incomplete' badge, a 44px amber '+ Add parent contact' button, amber 'Waiting N days' chips, and a two-line amber sentence repeated verbatim on every row that carries it. Read at a squint the right column is a stripe of warn from top to bottom, so amber has stopped meaning 'this one needs fixing' and become the column's house colour. It also inverts a card: the loudest object inside 'New faces' is the amber CTA, not the two students, so a card about good news reads as a warning — while the tile 40px above it colours the same two students present-green. Same students, two accents, two feet apart, and the reader has to work out that they are not two populations. Stacking these four cards has made the overlap visible in a way the old single scroll hid: Selah Mbeki and Jayden Rivers are in the top two cards, Bree Sandoval and Tomas Vielle in the second and fourth, so four ruled cards read as one list of the same seven people re-sorted four times.
evidence: 'New faces' contains, per row, a name, a grade, a date line, an amber badge and an amber button that is taller than the name is tall — two of them fill the card. 'Met once, never since' repeats 'Planning Center has no parent contact for <name>. Nobody can follow up until somebody adds one there.' in warn-400 on both of its two rows, naming the student it sits directly beneath, and the same sentence appears a third time in 'Missing in action' in the left column. The only non-amber accents in the column are two brand 'Visitor' pills and two danger 'Waiting 329 days' chips.
direction: Pick one carrier for 'no parent contact' and use it once per row. The badge is enough where the row is about something else; the button belongs where fixing it is the job — the 'Incomplete profiles' card — not in the card about new arrivals, which should be allowed to read as good news the tile above already says it is. The repeated sentence is a row *state*, not a message: said once per row in a two-row card it is the card's body copy, and it should be said once by the card, or reduced to the same badge everything else uses. If the four cards really are mostly one population, the column has just shown you that, and it is a grouping question, not a styling one.

where: the 28rem right column — the 'Copy list' button and the meta lines inside 'Met once, never since'
finding: The right column is narrower than the components put into it, and the components say so. 'Copy list' — the identical button that sits comfortably on one line in the left column's header 1,200px away — breaks to two lines inside its own pill, so a two-word label is stacked in a capsule. Two rows below it the same meta string truncates at two different points ('…Jul 10, 17 days a…' and '…Jul 10, 17 days …'), giving a two-row card a ragged pair of ellipses. Both of these are the exact defects round 1 named on the old 480px page and reported cured by the wider frame; they have simply moved into the right column. A component that sets correctly at 680px and breaks at 448px means the column was measured against its rows and not against its headers.
evidence: The two columns render at 682px and 450px with a 23px gutter. In the left column 'Copy list' is one line; in the right column, in a header that is otherwise identical, it is two.
direction: Either the right column takes the width its own cards need, or the cards that do not fit swap sides and the narrow column keeps only what is genuinely narrow — a name, a chip, a chevron. A label breaking inside its own button is the clearest possible signal that a column is 40px short; do not solve it by shortening the label.

where: the four stat tiles against the two columns beneath them
finding: The top of the page is on a different grid from the body. The tile row runs 6px gutters while everything below it — the columns, and the cards inside each column — runs 23–24px, so within one page frame the same kind of gap is set two ways and the four tiles fuse into one segmented bar rather than reading as four cards. Their seams agree with nothing: the tiles break at x≈541, 831 and 1121, and the body has one seam at x≈947, so no internal edge in the top 130px of the page lines up with any edge below it. The tiles also each took 284px and have no use for it — 'last 7 days' is about 60px of text in a 284px box — because the row's cells grew when the frame widened and its gutters stayed at their phone value.
evidence: Measured at y=210 the tiles occupy 255–538, 545–828, 835–1118, 1125–1408 (284px each, 6px apart). Measured at y=500 the columns occupy 255–936 and 959–1408 (23px apart).
direction: Give the tile row the page's gutter, and make its seams land on the body's, so there is one vertical seam running from the top of the page to the bottom instead of four that agree with nothing — three tiles over the left column and one over the right would do it, or scope the row to the left column entirely. Either way the row should look like it belongs to the same drawing as the cards.

where: the MIA / NEW FACES / INCOMPLETE tiles against the cards of the same names
finding: Three of the four tiles are now the headline of a card that is visible at the same time, with the same count and the same definition in almost the same words. 'NEW FACES 2 / last 7 days' sits about 40px above 'New faces 2 / First time in the last 7 days.'; 'INCOMPLETE 7 / no parent contact' sits above 'Incomplete profiles 7 / Active students with no parent phone or email on file.'; 'MIA 10 / 3+ missed in a row' sits above 'Missing in action 10 / Was a regular at one gathering, then missed 3 or more of it in a row.' A summary row earns its place by summarising something you cannot see; the split shortened the page enough that each tile is now a caption for the thing directly underneath it, and the reader reads every number twice before reaching a name. 'Last gathering, 16 · -2 vs 18 before' is the one tile that survives the comparison, because it is the only one carrying a fact no card below repeats.
evidence: All three counts and all three definitions appear twice above the fold in the same frame; the counts are even set in the same chip idiom on the card headers.
direction: Let the tiles carry what the cards cannot — a movement, a delta, a comparison against last time, the way 'Last gathering' already does — or drop the duplicated three and let the card headers, which already hold the counts, be the only place each number is stated. A row of four tiles is worth its 130px only if it answers something the page below does not.

where: the directory rows
finding: The dense single-line row is right, but widening the frame widened the gap rather than the information: the row now runs the full 1,152px carrying a name at the far left and a grade at the far right with about 820px of empty row between them, forty-five times. Round 1 complained that a chevron floated unmoored across 390px of nothing; the grade column has now joined it out there, across twice the distance. The result is that the list does not read as rows at all — it reads as a column of names and a separate column of grades that happen to share divider lines, and pairing the two costs an eye movement across the whole screen on every row.
evidence: Names begin at x=313 and 'Aisha Rahman' ends near x=440; the grade column begins at x≈1263 and the chevron sits at x=1392. Only five of the forty-five rows put anything in between, and those badges sit hard against the name, so the emptiness is unbroken for forty rows.
direction: Close the row. Either bring the grade in to a fixed distance from the longest name so the two facts read as one line and let the row end where its content ends, or spend the frame properly and set the directory in two columns of rows side by side — this is not the roster, a mis-tap here opens a neighbour's record rather than filing a check-in wrongly, and thirty names above the fold would be worth having. What the row must not stay is two words at opposite ends of a laptop.

where: the 'Incomplete profiles (5)' / 'Visitors (5)' chips in the Students toolbar, and the '+' square beside the roster search field
finding: Round 1 pulled three stacked rows of controls into one toolbar, which was the right move, but two controls did not take the pointer-size step the rest did, so the band it produced has two heights. The header buttons render at 38px and the search field and both selects at 39px; the two filter chips render at 46px. Bottom-aligned, they stand 7px proud of the toolbar's top line and end up the tallest objects in the row — a filter reading heavier than 'New visitor' directly above it, and the set of four controls that was meant to look like a set reading as three plus one. The same slip put a 48px square '+' beside a 40px search field on the roster, where the button that round 1 moved into the band overhangs the field it is paired with by 8px.
evidence: Students toolbar measured top-to-bottom: buttons 23–60, fields 117–155, chips 110–155. Roster band: field 182–220, '+' 172–219. The roster button does carry the compact pointer variant, but the plain size rule is declared after it in the overrides block and wins, so it draws at its touch size on a pointer screen.
direction: One control height per band at pointer sizes — the chips and the quick-add square need the same compact step the buttons, inputs and selects already take, and the roster override needs to lose to the variant rather than beat it. If a chip is meant to carry more weight than the field beside it, make that decision in colour or fill; being the one control that did not shrink is not a decision, it is a leftover.
